assessment_unit: Conditional benchmark review predicate at a selected source location, with surrounding source/caller evidence. Not a vulnerability, CVE, exploit, or native-rule accuracy adjudication.

current_ledger_correspondence.changed_provenance_retained: Current Invarune tool/report version metadata differs; original audit rows retain their frozen historical metadata. These are corresponding source observations, not a rerun of adjudication.

definitions.conditional_rule_mismatch: Context contradicts the benchmark conditional security predicate, such as a public key, placeholder, error label, environment-variable name, or local self-install reference. Native lexical matching can remain valid. This is not automatically a native-scanner false positive.
definitions.insufficient_evidence: Available source could not establish or refute the source predicate. Runtime uncertainty is separately preserved in vulnerability_status.
definitions.not_established: No vulnerability was established, including where source context reduces concern. This is not a verified security pass.
definitions.requires_runtime_validation: A meaningful deployment/trust-boundary question remains; no vulnerability was confirmed.
definitions.supported_source_pattern: The described API/configuration pattern is visible in verified source context. It may be intentional, mitigated, default-disabled, a safe use, or irrelevant to a deployed threat boundary. It is not a vulnerability true positive.

evidence_provenance.verification: Every cited file was read locally and its SHA-256 and Git blob hash verified against benchmarks/real-world/snapshots/<project>.json; revision and source-manifest digest were matched to the frozen observation ledger. Export directories have no independent Git checkout, so their enclosing workspace HEAD is not used as target revision evidence.

limitations: Purposive subset: all 28 Invarune observations in the parent selection are deliberately included. The 50 observations are not a representative precision sample and tools have different predicates/denominators. Do not rank tools from these counts.

No independent human ground truth, no Claude adjudication, no target execution, no exploitation, no model-mediated attack testing, no credential validity checks and no deployed service requests occurred.
API-pattern support is not vulnerability precision. Multiple tools at one location are multiple observations of the same code, not multiple vulnerabilities or independent confirmation.

Runtime exposure, effective identity/authorization, data provenance, filesystem permissions, dependency CVEs and deployed artifact configuration were not established. Source defaults and apparent mitigations are not verified deployment safeguards.

The source export deliberately excludes CI workflows, documentation trees, tests and other scopes described by the public-project manifest. Absence in this export is not absence from the repository. No recall or false-negative rate can be inferred without separately finding vulnerabilities in unflagged code.

The frozen ledger identifies Invarune observations as version 0.9.0 even though the surrounding release work is 0.10.0. These observations retain their original IDs, versions, hashes and conditional predicates; this audit does not relabel a different scan as the frozen run.

Three Dockerfile observations refer to a preceding blank line. Their actual FROM instructions are cited separately and their source pattern remains supported; this is a location-quality defect, not a missing detection.

observations.proposed_action: Check directory ownership, write permissions, and any memory-import paths; prefer a data-only serialization format or enforce trusted storage before loading existing memory files.
